subject: general
question: How did the Industrial Revolution alter the British economic interests in India?

options.text: From trade to industry and raw material use

solution:
The correct answer is __**From trade to industry and raw material use**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the Industrial Revolution, British economic interests in India shifted from simply trading finished goods to exploiting India as a source of raw materials like cotton and jute.
 
• The British established industries in England that required raw materials from colonies like India, leading to the development of plantation agriculture and mining in India.
 
• India became a supplier of raw materials for British industries and a market for British manufactured goods, leading to the decline of indigenous industries like textiles.
 
• The British also built infrastructure such as railways and ports, primarily to facilitate the transportation of raw materials and finished goods, serving their industrial needs.
 
• The economic policies were designed to benefit Britain, extracting wealth from India and suppressing its economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Revolution:**

 
 
• Began in Britain in the late 18th century and marked a shift from agrarian economies to industrialized ones.
 
• Required vast quantities of raw materials, driving colonial exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Plantation Agriculture:**
 
 
• Focused on crops like cotton, jute, and indigo, which were exported to Britain.
 
• Disrupted traditional farming practices and led to exploitation of labor.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Indian Textiles:**
 
 
• Indian textile industry suffered as British imported cheap, machine-made goods.
 
• Indian artisans and craftsmen faced economic ruin due to competition with British goods.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure Development:**
 
 
• Railways were built by the British primarily to transport goods rather than for public welfare.
 
• Ports like Mumbai and Kolkata were developed as trade hubs to serve British interests.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Economic Policies:**
 
 
• Policies were heavily skewed towards maximizing British profits at the expense of Indian economic growth.
 
• Led to widespread poverty and economic stagnation in India during British rule.
